concepts.def: First number tugs all later estimates

walkthroughs.body_html:
Daniel Kahneman (2011) distinguished two systems.

System 1 — fast, automatic, uses heuristics; great for skilled rapid judgement.

System 2 — slow, effortful, statistical reasoning; rarely engaged unless prompted.

Most biases arise when System 1 answers a question System 2 should.

Anchoring (Tversky & Kahneman, 1974): a random spin of a wheel of fortune influenced estimates of African UN members.

Availability: people overrate plane crash risk because vivid examples come easily.

Confirmation bias (Wason 1960, 2-4-6 task): testing ideas you already believe.

Strategies: pre-commit to criteria, seek disconfirming evidence (Popper), use base rates, slow down with checklists (Gawande).

Group debiasing: 'red teams', devil's advocate, decision pre-mortems (Klein, 2007).
